Structure Your Prompt

Looking for prompt best practices? See the [Prompting Guide](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/developer-guide/build/agent-crews/llm/prompts) for voice-specific techniques, common mistakes, and a complete example blueprint.

## Structure Your Prompt

Cover seven things in your prompt:

- **Role & Objective.** Who is this agent and what’s their goal?
- **Personality & Tone.** How should they sound? Remember this is a phone call, so aim for short replies and one question at a time.
- **Product Knowledge.** What should the agent know cold, without guessing?
- **Instructions.** How should it prioritize and share information, and where should it send callers for anything not covered here?
- **Conversation Flow.** What steps should the call follow?
- **Guardrails.** What should the agent never do?
- **Tools.** For each tool you enable on the [Tools tab](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/tools/agent-tools-tab), when should the agent use it?

**Product Knowledge vs. Knowledge Base.** Small, stable facts, like what your product does or how your pricing works, belong directly in the prompt so the agent always has them on hand. Large or frequently changing content, like manuals or help docs, belongs in a [Knowledge Base](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/knowledge-base) instead.

## Jump Between Sections

Click the sections icon (a bulleted list) in the prompt toolbar to jump to any heading in your prompt. Useful once your prompt gets long.

## Model Selection

The model is your agent’s brain. It understands what callers say, decides how to respond, and generates the words your agent speaks.

**Location:** **Prompt** tab → **Model**

| Model | Provider | Group | Credit usage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Electron** | Smallest AI | Traditional Models | Lower |
| **GPT-4o** | OpenAI | Traditional Models | Moderate |
| **GPT 4.1** | OpenAI | Traditional Models | Moderate |
| **GPT Realtime** | OpenAI | Emotional Models | Higher |
| **GPT Realtime Mini** | OpenAI | Emotional Models | Higher |

Emotional models are speech-to-speech: they pick up on caller tone and respond with natural expression. Some organizations have extra models enabled, such as GPT 5.2. A model is greyed out if it doesn’t support every language you’ve added.

Getting started? **GPT-4o** is a reliable all-rounder. For voice specifically, **Electron** (our own model) is the overall best choice: see its [benchmarks and model card](https://docs.smallest.ai/model-cards/llm/electron). Electron is available on the **Enterprise plan** only; [contact sales](https://smallest.ai/book-a-demo) to get access.

You can switch models at any time. Switching between an emotional and a traditional model asks you to confirm first, because it changes the voice configuration.

* * *

## Languages

**Location:** **Prompt** tab → **Languages**

The language marked **Primary** is the one the agent starts in. Click **Add a language** to add others the agent can switch to during a call. A language’s menu has **Set as primary** and **Remove language**. An agent always keeps at least one language. Languages tagged **Beta** are still in beta.

With more than one language added, the card shows **Language switching enabled**: the agent detects and switches between your languages during a conversation.

Which languages the agent can use depends on its STT model, model, and voice. See [Supported languages](https://docs.smallest.ai/voice-agents/build/agent-settings#supported-languages) for the full list.

* * *

## Voice Selection

Your agent’s voice is often the first thing callers notice. A voice that fits your brand builds trust before your prompt says a word.

**Location:** **Prompt** tab → **Voice**

| Section | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Search voices** | Find voices by name or characteristic |
| **Filters** | Narrow by **Languages**, **Gender**, **Accent**, **Age**, or **Model** |
| **Recommended** | When you filter by one language, voices for that language are listed under **Recommended**, with other voices that also support it under **Also supported** |

Below the voice, choose the voice model (for example **Lightning V3.1 Pro**).

**Always preview.** Click the play button next to any voice to hear a sample. Listen with your prompt in mind, does this voice sound like the agent you’ve written?
